title: Different models, different tradeoffs.
description: How you get software shapes what happens next. Explore how different approaches compare in flexibility, time, effort, and ongoing responsibility.
disclaimer: Illustrative comparison of typical delivery models. Values are qualitative, not measured benchmarks, pricing estimates, or performance guarantees. Actual outcomes depend on scope and implementation.

dimensions.title: Operational fit
dimensions.question: How closely does the software fit the way your business actually works?
dimensions.description: The ability to accommodate your company's specific processes, relationships, rules, and requirements.

superspace.explanation: Configured around your operational model on a managed platform.

saas.explanation: Designed for standardized use cases, with customization options that vary by product.

consulting.explanation: Custom software can be designed around highly specific business requirements.

internal.explanation: Internal teams can build software directly around organizational requirements.

dimensions.title: Time to first working version
dimensions.question: How long does it take to get a working system into your team's hands?
dimensions.description: The typical time required to go from initial engagement to an operational first version.

superspace.explanation: Focused discovery and configuration accelerate delivery without requiring a new codebase.

saas.explanation: Standard functionality can often be deployed quickly when it already fits the business.

consulting.explanation: Custom design, development, testing, and delivery typically require a longer implementation cycle.

internal.explanation: Staffing, planning, engineering, and deployment can extend the time before the first working version.

dimensions.title: Upfront deployment effort
dimensions.question: How much work is required to get the initial system running?
dimensions.description: The organizational and technical effort needed to implement a solution before it becomes operational.

superspace.explanation: Your team participates in discovery and validation while SuperSpace handles configuration and deployment.

saas.explanation: Standard use cases often require relatively little setup, although complex implementations can demand more.

consulting.explanation: Custom projects require substantial scoping, coordination, design, development, and validation.

internal.explanation: Your organization must resource and coordinate the entire implementation process.

dimensions.title: Ongoing technical burden
dimensions.question: How much technical responsibility does your team carry after launch?
dimensions.description: The ongoing internal effort required to operate, maintain, update, and support the software.

superspace.explanation: SuperSpace hosts, operates, maintains, and updates the underlying platform.

saas.explanation: The software provider generally handles maintenance and updates for its standard application.

consulting.explanation: Ongoing maintenance depends on the delivery agreement and may require additional support contracts.

internal.explanation: Your team typically remains responsible for infrastructure, engineering, maintenance, and technical continuity.

dimensions.title: Effort to accommodate change
dimensions.question: How much effort does it take to adapt the system as your business changes?
dimensions.description: The effort required to adapt workflows, introduce new capabilities, or accommodate evolving operational requirements.

superspace.explanation: Many changes can be addressed through configuration. Larger extensions are evaluated and scoped separately.

saas.explanation: Requirements outside the product's existing capabilities may require workarounds, integrations, or additional tools.

consulting.explanation: New requirements frequently become additional development projects with separate scope and costs.

internal.explanation: Changes can be implemented internally but compete for engineering capacity and ongoing maintenance resources.
